premises: Acid-etching dealloying can selectively leach less noble elements from a multi-element alloy to form a noble-metal-enriched shell.
A Pt-rich shell on a high-entropy alloy core improves catalytic activity and durability by adjusting adsorption energies and suppressing poisoning.
The formation of stable M–N bonds (e.g., Ni–N, Co–N) in the shell suppresses dissolution of transition metals and enhances durability.
A core–shell structure with a Pt-rich surface and high-entropy core can be synthesized and is beneficial for electrocatalytic performance.
